A Notable Stop, but the Michelin Magic Didn’t Quite Land
Nov 2025 • Friends
Pho Viet Nam in Ho Chi Minh City is undeniably a destination spot, the kind of place travelers seek out because of its Michelin star rather than because a local nudged them there. I visited at the very start of my Vietnam trip, which ended up being helpful—I had a well-recognized version of pho to compare against everything else I tried along the way.

Service is quick and efficient, and the broth is clean, flavorful, and well crafted. But beyond that, not much else signaled a Michelin-level experience for me. It was good pho, but not transformative pho.

A couple of notes: the Chinese fried bread costs extra, and the stone hot pot option—while dramatic—is more gimmick than enhancement. Skip the theatrics and go for the simple bowl.

I’m glad I tried it, especially as a benchmark, but whatever magic the guide recognized didn’t quite translate to my visit. It's a solid stop, just not the standout I had hoped for.

Seating Upstairs Quieter and Entertaining
Oct 2025 • Family
When we first arrived, the restaurant was full and we were walked over to their second location. However when the person left us there, the second location came back and told us they were also full so we were escorted back to the main one. Geez.

The first location finally decided to bring us upstairs to an empty floor and we got seated by the window overlooking the Main Street. Not sure why they didn’t just do that when we first arrived.

I must admit the second floor window seats were some of the best as we got a snapshot view of everyday life and traffic in HCM. Families riding on one scooter, trash collection, arguments about traffic, food sellers moving their carts, people cautiously crossing the road with no crosswalks and so on. Also oddly enough no other customers were brought upstairs so it was like having the whole place to ourselves and so much quieter than the first floor.

The menu had a nice variety of different meat types (ie. flank, oxtail, beef balls) served with their pho. A few also could be ordered in different sizes.

I got the beef flank bowl and was served with generous amounts of meat. The flank was a little pink, tender and thickly sliced. The broth was tasty and the noodles were nice and chewy. Overall a hearty meal for just 85000 dong. 

Service was as expected after the initial ping pong between locations. We just paid our bill at the cashier downstairs. There was no check left at the table but the the cashier knew what we ordered (maybe since we were the only ones upstairs).

Definitely would come back here again if I’m back in HCM.
